To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
environmental and handling stress induce biochemical changes in the muscle proteomes of channel catfish that affect fillet quality.
environmental and handling stressors affect the quality of catfish fillets by altering the abundance of structural and regulatory proteins and by inducing proteolytic activity in the muscle tissue.
the muscle proteome of catfish was altered by the stress induced by temperature and oxygen levels, and that the severity of the changes was dependent on the severity of the applied stress.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of ante-mortem stress on the quality of channel catfish.
the impact of environmental and handling conditions during the aquaculture of catfish and the changes in the proteome profile of the muscle.
the effects of stress during the culture of channel catfish on muscle proteome and fillet quality.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the stressors evaluated in this study did not affect the quality of the fillets in a negative way.
hypoxia is the most detrimental of the factors studied in this work.

the handling stress and the environmental factors (temperature, hypoxia, and hyperoxia) have an impact on the muscle proteome, which could be responsible for changes in the color and texture of channel catfish fillet.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fish subjected to severe stress (33-H-S) had the highest proteolytic activity, which could have contributed to the observed changes in color and texture.
the changes in the proteome profile and the quality of fillet are dependent upon the type of stressor and the severity of stress.
handling stressors can be managed by controlling environmental conditions and that the proteome can be used as a tool to assess the quality of the product.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the muscle proteome is sensitive to stress and that it is possible to manipulate stress conditions to produce fish fillets of desired quality.
the handling of fish during aquaculture has an effect on fillet quality.
the stressors applied to the catfish during aquaculture have significant impacts on muscle proteome and fillet quality.
